h: Little Legs, Big Day: Planning Your Tilgate Trip
p: Tilgate Zoo works best when you treat it as part of a whole day in the park. Get to the zoo early while the little ones are fresh, then spend the afternoon picnicking by the lakes or exploring the woods. That way nobody gets bored and you get the best out of both.

Many of the animals here are rare or traditional breeds, and the zoo has a real focus on conservation. Ask the keepers about the rare-breed farm animals in particular, as many are old British breeds that have become scarce, and it's a great chance for kids to learn where some of our heritage animals come from. The setting is green and relaxed, so it's a lovely first zoo trip for toddlers.

Wear sensible footwear, as some paths can be muddy after rain, and bring a waterproof just in case. The park has car parks, but they fill up quickly on sunny weekends and in the school holidays, so it's worth arriving early. Bear in mind too that the walled garden and lakes are popular with dog walkers, so the park can be busy even when the zoo is quieter.

Crawley's surroundings offer plenty more. Wakehurst, Kew's wild botanic garden near Ardingly, is a short drive away, with woodland walks, glasshouses and the Millennium Seed Bank. Steam fans will love the Bluebell Railway, which runs vintage trains through the Sussex countryside between East Grinstead and Sheffield Park. And if the kids are into planes, Gatwick Airport is right on Crawley's doorstep, so you'll often see aircraft coming in overhead.
